Kavak Card for Draiver Operators - 2026/09/29 12:30 CST - Notes by Gemini
Sep 29, 2026
Invited: Kevin Burke (kevin.burke@driverdo.com), Fede Ranero (fede.ranero@driverdo.com), Armando Flores (armando.flores@driverdo.com), dario.mattio@kavak.com, Paulo Ferrato (paulo.ferrato@driverdo.com), federico.boero@kavak.com

### Summary
Financial providers reviewed and Mexican operational challenges addressed via parallel testing approved.
Regional Revenue And Providers: US accounts for 90 percent of revenue while international operations face tax deduction losses. Current financial partners include Ramp, PEX, Airbase, and Car IQ.
Mexican Operational Challenges: Mexico operations represent half of marketplace volume with significant tax losses from non-deductible foreign cards. Evaluation of Mendel and in-house Kavak cards provides potential solutions.
Technical Architecture And Testing: Contract with Mendel approved at zero cost for parallel testing alongside the Kavak card integration. Technical teams aligned on API evaluations and merchant category code controls.

### Decisions
Aligned
- Adoption of Kavak Card Solution: move forward with the in-house Kavak card rather than Mendel for managing driver expenses.
- Scheduling Technical Integration Meeting: Darío Mattio will schedule a technical meeting with Kevin Burke and team to review documentation and APIs for the Kavak card integration.

### Next steps
- [Kevin Burke] Review API Specifications: Review Pomelo integration documentation and Mendel API specifications to evaluate compatibility with the Kavak card system.
- [Federico Boero, Darío Mattio] Provide CLI Access: Grant access to the Kavak command line interface to facilitate technical evaluation and integration.
- [Armando Flores] Test Mendel Cards: Execute a pilot program using Mendel cards for corporate travel expenses and a limited group of drivers. Monitor performance to validate tax deductibility and integration functionality.
- [Federico Boero] Schedule Technical Call: Schedule a follow-up technical meeting to discuss integration requirements and build the card operational solution for drivers.
- [Darío Mattio] Coordinate Technical Call: Discuss the use case requirements with the internal technical team. Arrange a subsequent meeting with the external parties involved.
- [Kevin Burke] Review API Documentation: Utilize AI tools to compare the provided documentation with the existing PEX implementation. Flag necessary technical items for further evaluation.

### Details
Revenue: US is 90% of revenue; Mexico and Brazil 7-10% depending on month; Mexico is half of marketplace moves by volume.
Providers: Ramp (driver flights/hotels, 30-day credit, 1.5% cashback); PEX (prepaid physical fuel cards with real-time customer decisioning API; ~3% total cost internationally); Airbase (subscriptions, leadership cards, no credit, may consolidate into Ramp); Car IQ (fuel pilot in Detroit/Chicago, acquired by Element Fleet Management); Brazil local card; customer credit card billing (e.g. Penske) to get cash in 3 days vs 60.
Mexico problems (Armando): PEX not accepted in ~50% of Mexican terminals; foreign card expenses not tax-deductible (~$5k-$20k/month lost deductions); physical card logistics. Mendel chosen for local virtual cards, APIs and AI receipt scanning to generate facturas.
Kavak card (Federico Boero): already operating in Mexico with employees, virtual and physical, >85% approval rate, Google/Apple Pay tokenization; not yet a mature B2B product (no back office for expense reports) but can move fast.
Testing: Paulo — Mendel contract approved at zero commitment; test both in parallel. Armando suggested testing Mendel on corporate travel (Armando, Julia) first; Fede asked that tests be representative of driver spend (fuel, tolls, bus tickets). Paulo stressed Mexico is a major finance bottleneck and must move fast.
Architecture: Mendel uses Pomelo, same processor as Kavak. Kavak/Pomelo can block MCCs (e.g. gas stations only) and turn cards on/off; real-time authorization not yet but small effort. Kavak CLI can create cards, set lines, switch on/off, pull transactions. Kevin: integration needs only create card, authorize transaction, close card; prefers in-house Kavak card. Armando: move forward with Kavak; use Mendel (no cost, includes travel platform) for other things. Brazil not supported locally; focus is Mexico.
